To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inhibition within the trigeminothalamic system is important in determining the response range of mechanosensitive neurone activity.
the inhibition within the trigemino-cortical pathway is a significant factor in determining the response properties of the neurones.

inhibition within the trigemino-cervical nucleus induced by a peripheral afferent input can have a profound effect on the response of the neurones to natural stimulation and that this effect can vary from one neurone to another and from one stimulus to another.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of inhibition within the trigemino-cerebellar system and its influence on the processing of sensory information.
the mechanisms of pain and nociception in the trigemino-cervical nucleus, with particular reference to the role of the trigeminothalamic tract.
the mechanisms underlying the control of motor activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition is not a significant factor in the coding of stimulus intensity and direction by these neurones.

, for neurones in the nucleus oralis of decerebrate, non-anaesthetized cat, inhibition within the trigemino-thalamic system has a profound and significant influence on the coding of the mechanical properties of natural stimulation of their receptive fields.

, in the absence of inhibition, these neurones respond to natural stimulation with a pattern of activity which is consistent with the known properties of the receptors and the peripheral structures they innervate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

inhibition of these neurones by conditioning stimuli applied within the trigemino-facial field is not a general feature of their stimulus coding, but that it does influence the coding in some neurones.
inhibition is a powerful mechanism that can profoundly affect the coding properties of these neurones.

the inhibition was not a significant factor in stimulus coding for most neurones, but that in the minority of cases where it did affect stimulus coding it was not a simple inhibitory effect, but rather a complex phenomenon that could either increase or decrease the sensitivity of the neurone to a stimulus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibition was not an artefact of the stimulus protocol.

, when we are able to control for afferent inputs, inhibition does not appear to have a substantial impact on the coding of mechanical information by mechanosensitive cells in the trigemino-cerebral pathway.
the trigeminal sensory system is not only capable of encoding the intensity and location of mechanical stimuli but is also well-suited for the encoding of the temporal pattern of the stimulus.
